## Summary of Results

Catherine Connolly, an independent TD and former Leas-Cheann Comhairle, representing the left/progressive wing, won the 2025 Irish presidential election. 

**Final Results:**
- Catherine Connolly (Independent): 63.4% (914,143 votes)
- Heather Humphreys (Fine Gael): 29.5% (424,987 votes)
- Jim Gavin (Fianna Fáil): 7.2% (103,568 votes)

The election took place on October 24, 2025, with vote counting concluding on October 25. Connolly has been outspoken in criticising Israel over its war in Gaza and had garnered the backing of a range of left-leaning parties, including Sinn Fein, the Labour Party and the Social Democrats.

## Summary of 2025 Irish Presidential Election Results

Independent candidate Catherine Connolly, backed by left-wing parties, won Ireland's presidential election on 24 October. Connolly won 63.36% of first-preference votes, ahead of Heather Humphreys (Fine Gael), who won 29.46%.

This means that Catherine Connolly has won the election by the largest margin ever recorded in an Irish presidential election. Connolly secured 914,143 votes, more than double Humphreys' 424,987.

The former Deputy Speaker of the Dail Eireann, the lower house of parliament (2010-2024), won the election, and will serve as the country's 10th president. Of the 3,612,957 people eligible to vote, 1,656,436 cast their vote in the 2025 presidential election, representing a turnout of 46%.
